content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (critical) — Section 14.2, Deliverable ownership.**

- **Compliant elsewhere:** § 14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP with no transfer to Vendor; § 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology but routes it through the § 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence; § 14.4 bars joint ownership; § 15.1 blocks model training on Customer Data.
- **The failure:** § 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer, with only a *revocable, non-transferable, Order Form–term* licence back. That fails not just the preferred position but the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense. § 13.2 does not rescue it — that licence reaches only Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** flips § 14.2 to Customer ownership with an express Vendor assignment on creation, while expressly preserving Vendor Technology under § 14.3 so Vendor's platform rights are untouched. The licence-back fallback is offered in the comment as the compromise landing zone.
